title: 1. A first web page
summary: Headings and paragraphs: the words a page shows.

steps.title: A heading
steps.instructions:
A web page is made of tags. Put the words My first page between

and

to make a heading.

steps.title: A paragraph under it
steps.instructions:
Keep the heading. Under it add a paragraph with

and

that says: I am learning HTML.
steps.expectedOutput:
My first page
I am learning HTML.

steps.title: A smaller heading
steps.instructions: Keep both. Add a smaller heading with <h2> that says About me, and under it a paragraph that says I like to build things.
steps.expectedOutput:
My first page
I am learning HTML.
About me
I like to build things.

title: 2. Lists and links
summary: Putting things in a list, and linking to another page.

steps.title: A list of three
steps.instructions: Start a new page. Make a heading <h1> that says My favourite fruits. Under it make a list: <ul> around the whole list, and <li> around each of Apple, Banana and Mango.
steps.expectedOutput:
My favourite fruits
Apple
Banana
Mango

steps.title: A numbered list
steps.instructions: Change <ul> to <ol>, and its closing tag too. The page now numbers the fruits by itself. The numbers are drawn by the browser, so the words on the page stay the same.
steps.expectedOutput:
My favourite fruits
Apple
Banana
Mango

steps.title: A link
steps.instructions: Under the list add a paragraph holding a link. A link is Learn Python: the address goes in href, and the words between the tags are what the page shows.
steps.expectedOutput:
My favourite fruits
Apple
Banana
Mango
Learn Python

title: 3. Colour and size with CSS
summary: Styling a page. The words are checked; the colours are for the eye.

steps.title: A page to style
steps.instructions:
Start a new page with a heading

that says Hello and a paragraph

that says This page has style.

steps.title: Colour the heading
steps.instructions: Above the heading add <style> and </style>. Between them write a rule: h1 { color: tomato; } The heading turns red. Only the words can be checked, so look at your page to see that it worked.

steps.title: Style the paragraph too
steps.instructions: Add a second rule inside <style>: p { font-size: 24px; color: steelblue; } Then try other colours and sizes of your own.

title: 4. First JavaScript
summary: Making the page calculate, and reading its console.

steps.title: Say hello in the console
steps.instructions: JavaScript goes between <script> and </script>. Write console.log("Hello"); there. The console under your page shows what it prints.

steps.title: Let JavaScript do the sum
steps.instructions: Print the result of 6 times 7 with console.log, without typing the answer yourself. Use * to multiply.

steps.title: A variable
steps.instructions: Make a variable with let name = "Asha"; and print a greeting that uses it, so the console shows the line below.

steps.title: Ask a question
steps.instructions: prompt() asks the person a question and gives back what they type. Ask for a name with prompt("Your name?") and print a greeting for it. When this step is checked, the answer below is typed for you.

title: 5. Choosing with if and else
summary: JavaScript that does one thing or another.

steps.title: Pass or fail
steps.instructions: Ask for marks with prompt(). What comes back is text, so wrap it in Number() to get a number. If the marks are 40 or more print Pass with console.log, otherwise print Fail.

steps.title: The other side
steps.instructions: Do not change your page. Check it again here, where the marks are 20. A page that only ever prints Pass will not get through this step.

steps.title: Even or odd
steps.instructions: Ask for a whole number. Print Even if it divides by 2 with nothing left over, otherwise print Odd. The % sign gives the remainder of a division.

title: 6. JavaScript changes the page
summary: Loops, and writing onto the page from a script.

steps.title: Count to five
steps.instructions: Print the numbers 1 to 5 in the console, one on each line, with a for loop: for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { ... }

steps.title: Write onto the page
steps.instructions:
Start a new page with

Old words

. Under it, in a script, change the heading: document.getElementById("title").textContent = "New words"; The page now shows the new words.

steps.title: Greet by name on the page
steps.instructions: Keep the heading with id="title". Ask for a name with prompt() and put a greeting for it into the heading, so the page shows the line below.
